correctness.rationale: For n=1..10, the included exhaustive C++ algorithm loops over every 2n-bit word index induced by every size-n position mask and every n-bit root, marks a bit iff the output is the shuffle of that root and its reverse, and takes exact popcounts/maxima. The proof shows the loops cover both directions of the root definition, so the maximum is exact on the finite domain. Recompiled actual program produced M=1,2,3,5,9,16,29,52,94,170 and optimizer counts 2,4,8,...,8. n=10 covered exactly 184756 masks and 189190144 root-mask pairs. Independent Python direct-word/partition enumeration agreed for n<=6, 170 explicit supports were checked, and the global count of nonempty-root words independently matched binom(2n,n) for every n<=10. No infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is the complete sharp inverse ambiguity invariant for reverse shuffle-square generation on the first ten binary root lengths, culminating in the full 1,048,576-source-word universe at length 20. It gives both the previously unstated maximum (170) and all eight optimizers, not just one witness or code correctness. The inverse-root multiplicity problem is directly motivated by current research on shuffle-square root counts; the 2025 ordinary root maximum is only 19 at the same length, demonstrating a mathematically substantial distinction between two natural generating relations. The exact optimizer census and witness data give substantive boundary information for future structural work rather than an arbitrary small sample.
